name: Letter Series — Alphabet Patterns
whatIsIt: A letter series is a number series in disguise. Give every letter its position number (A=1, B=2, C=3 … Z=26), and the alphabet pattern becomes an ordinary number pattern you already know how to solve. Then translate the answer position back into a letter.
whyNeeded: Letter and alpha-numeric series appear in almost every reasoning paper. Once you use the A=1…Z=26 table, they stop being scary — they are just 'add' or 'skip' patterns on positions.
realLifeUses: Reasoning sections of SSC / Bank / Railway exams
Spotting patterns in labels and part numbers
Building the base skill for coding-decoding

vocabulary.meaning: The place of a letter in the alphabet: A=1, B=2 … Z=26.
How many letters you jump each step (A, C, E skips 2).
After Z you go back to A (Z=26, then A=1 again).

story.title: Letters Are Just Numbers Wearing Hats
story.text: Ravi is stuck on A, C, E, G, __. His sister writes the positions: A=1, C=3, E=5, G=7. 'See? 1, 3, 5, 7 — odd numbers, skip 2. Next is 9, and the 9th letter is I.' Ravi grins: 'So letters are just numbers wearing hats!' She adds one rule: 'After Z (26) you wrap back to A.' Now Ravi turns every letter series into a number series first.
story.extractedProblem: What comes next: A, C, E, G, __ ?
story.answerInStory: I — positions are 1, 3, 5, 7 (skip 2), next position 9 = the letter I.

visual.caption: A=1, C=3, E=5, G=7. As positions it's 1,3,5,7 (skip 2). Next position 9 = the letter I.

teachingGallery.title: Turn letters into positions, solve, translate back
teachingGallery.note: A=1 … Z=26. Solve the number pattern, then map the answer number to its letter.

standardMethod.summary: Write A=1…Z=26 positions under the letters, solve the number pattern, then convert the answer position back to a letter (wrapping after 26).
steps: Write each letter's position number (A=1, B=2 … Z=26).
Find the number pattern (usually a constant skip).
Extend the pattern to the next position number.
Convert that position back to a letter; if it goes past 26, wrap around (27→A).

alternateMethods.name: Count on your fingers
alternateMethods.whenToUse: Small skips, no need to write positions.
steps: Say the alphabet and physically skip the pattern.
A … (skip B) C … (skip D) E — the skip of 2 is easy to feel.
alternateMethods.example: A, C, E, G → keep skipping one letter → I.

commonMistakes.mistake: Guessing letters directly and losing count in the middle of the alphabet.
commonMistakes.fix: Write A=1…Z=26 (or at least count carefully). Turning letters into numbers removes almost all the guesswork.

commonMistakes.mistake: Getting stuck when the pattern goes past Z, or past A when counting backwards.
commonMistakes.fix: Wrap around: after Z (26) comes A (1) again; before A comes Z. Treat the alphabet as a loop.

teachBackPrompt: Show a friend how to solve A, C, E, G by writing positions 1, 3, 5, 7 → next 9 → I. Explain the A=1…Z=26 table and the wrap-around rule after Z.

revisionCard.summary: Letter series = number series in disguise. Write A=1…Z=26 positions, solve the (usually constant-skip) number pattern, then translate the next position back to a letter. Wrap around after Z (27→A). Backwards series just subtract.

gameMission.title: Alphabet Decoder
gameMission.brief: Convert letters to positions, crack the skip, and name the next letter! Remember to wrap past Z back to A.

realLifeProject: Write your name, replace each letter with its position number, and challenge a friend to decode it back. Then make one letter-series puzzle with a skip of 3.

rememberIt.unpack: Convert to positions, solve the skip pattern, translate back, wrap after Z.

studentQuestions.q: Do I have to memorise every position?
studentQuestions.a: It helps to know the anchors: A=1, E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Z=26. From an anchor you can count a few steps quickly.
You wrap around — after Z (26) comes A (1) again, like a loop. Counting backwards, before A comes Z.
